readings.title: Job Defends His Integrity
readings.subtitle: I Would Speak to the Almighty
readings.text: [Job 13:1] “See, my eye has seen all this, my ear has heard and understood it. [2] “What you know, I know also; I am not less than you. [3] “But I would speak to the <dn>Almighty</dn>, and I delight to reason with <dn>El</dn>. [4] “But you are forgers of lies, you are all worthlessness healers. [5] “If you would only keep completely silent! For it would be your wisdom. [6] “Hear now my reasoning, and listen to the pleadings of my lips. [7] “Would you speak unrighteousness for <dn>El</dn>, and talk deceit for <dn>Him</dn>? [8] “Would you show partiality for <dn>Him</dn>? Would you contend for <dn>El</dn>? [9] “Is it good that <dn>He</dn> should search <dn>את</dn> you out? Or as one mocks a man, do you mock <dn>Him</dn>? [10] “<dn>He</dn> would certainly reprove you if you secretly show partiality. [11] “Does not <dn>His</dn> excellence make you afraid? And the dread of <dn>Him</dn> fall upon you? [12] “Your remembrances are proverbs of ashes, your bodies are bodies of clay. [13] “Keep silent before me, and let me speak, and let come on me what might. [14] “Why do I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hands? [15] “See, <dn>He</dn> slays me – I wait for <dn>Him</dn>. Only, I argue my ways before <dn>His</dn> face. [16] “Even this is my deliverance, for a profane one does not come before <dn>Him</dn>. [17] “Listen closely to my speech, and let my declaration be in your ears. [18] “See now, I have prepared my case, I know that I am in the right. [19] “Who is he that contends with me? For then I would be silent and die.

readings.title: A Plea for Respite
readings.subtitle: Man Born of Woman is of Few Days
readings.text: [Job 13:20] “Only two things do not do to me, then I am not hidden from <dn>Your</dn> face: [21] “Withdraw <dn>Your</dn> hand far from me, and let not the dread of <dn>You</dn> make me afraid. [22] “Then call, and I answer; or let me speak, and <dn>You</dn> reply to me. [23] “How many are my crookednesses and sins? Make me know my transgression and my sin. [24] “Why do <dn>You</dn> hide <dn>Your</dn> face, and reckon me as <dn>Your</dn> enemy? [25] “Would <dn>You</dn> frighten a leaf driven to and fro? And pursue <dn>את</dn> dry stubble? [26] “For <dn>You</dn> write bitter things against me, and make me inherit the crookednesses of my youth. [27] “And <dn>You</dn> put my feet in the stocks, and watch closely all my paths. <dn>You</dn> set a limit for the soles of my feet. [28] “And he wears out like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten. [Job 14:1] “Man born of woman is of few days, and filled with trouble. [2] “He comes forth like a flower and fades away, and he flees like a shadow and does not stay. [3] “And on such a one <dn>You</dn> have opened <dn>Your</dn> eyes, and <dn>You</dn> bring <dn>את</dn> me into right-ruling with <dn>You</dn>. [4] “Who brings a clean one out of an unclean? No one! [5] “Since his days are decided, the number of his months is with <dn>You</dn>, <dn>You</dn> have appointed his limits which he does not pass. [6] “Look away from him and let him rest, till like a hireling he accomplishes his day. [7] “For there is hope for a tree, if it is cut down, that it sprouts again, and that its tender branches do not cease. [8] “Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stump dies in the dust, [9] “At the scent of water it buds and brings forth boughs like a plant. [10] “But man dies and is powerless; and man expires, and where is he? [11] “Water disappears from the sea, and a river becomes parched and dries up; [12] “So man lies down and does not rise. Till the heavens are no more, they do not awake nor are aroused from their sleep. [13] “Oh, that <dn>You</dn> would hide me in She’ol, would conceal me until <dn>Your</dn> wrath is past, that <dn>You</dn> would appoint me a set time, and remember me! [14] “If a man dies, does he live? All the days of my warfare I wait, till my change comes. [15] “<dn>You</dn> would call, and I would answer <dn>You</dn>. <dn>You</dn> would have a desire for the work of <dn>Your</dn> hands. [16] “For now <dn>You</dn> count my steps; <dn>You</dn> do not watch over my sin. [17] “My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and <dn>You</dn> cover over my crookedness. [18] “And truly, as a mountain falls and crumbles away, and as a rock is moved from its place; [19] “As water wears away stones, and as its torrents wash away the dust of the earth; so <dn>You</dn> have destroyed the expectation of man. [20] “<dn>You</dn> overpower him forever, and he passes away; <dn>You</dn> change his face and send him away. [21] “His sons come to honour, and he does not know it; and they are brought low, and he does not perceive it. [22] “But his flesh upon him is in pain, and his being within him mourns.”

readings.title: Eliphaz’s Second Rebuke
readings.subtitle: Your Own Mouth Condemns You
readings.text: [Job 15:1] Then Eliphaz the Têmanite answered and said, [2] “Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind? [3] “Reasoning with unprofitable talk, or with speeches which do no good? [4] “Truly, you do away with reverence, and diminish meditation before <dn>El</dn>. [5] “For your crookedness teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty. [6] “Your own mouth declares you wrong, and not I; and your own lips witness against you. [7] “Are you the first man to be born? Or were you brought forth before the hills? [8] “Have you heard the counsel of <dn>Eloah</dn>? And do you limit wisdom to yourself? [9] “What do you know that we do not know? Understand, that is not with us? [10] “Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, much older than your father. [11] “Are the consolations of <dn>El</dn> too small for you, and the word spoken gently with you? [12] “Why does your heart take you away? And why do your eyes flash? [13] “That you turn your spirit against <dn>El</dn>, and let words go out of your mouth? [14] “What is man, that he should be clean? And one born of woman, that he should be righteous? [15] “See, <dn>He</dn> puts no trust in <dn>His</dn> set-apart ones, and the heavens are not clean in <dn>His</dn> eyes. [16] “How much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a man drinking unrighteousness like water!

readings.title: The Fate of the Wicked
readings.subtitle: Distress and Anguish Terrify Him
readings.text: [Job 15:17] “I show you, listen to me; and this I have seen and declare, [18] “What wise men have told, from their fathers, and have not hidden, [19] “To whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed over in their midst: [20] “The wrong one is in pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden for the ruthless. [21] “A sound of fears is in his ears; in peace the ravager comes upon him. [22] “He does not believe that he will return from darkness, and he is watched for by the sword. [23] “He wanders about for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that a day of darkness is ready at his hand. [24] “Distress and anguish terrify him; they overpower him like a sovereign ready for battle. [25] “Because he has stretched out his hand against <dn>El</dn>, and acts mightily against the <dn>Almighty</dn>, [26] “He runs at <dn>Him</dn> with a stiff neck, with the thick bosses of his shields. [27] “Because he has covered his face with his fatness, and placed fat on his loins. [28] “And he dwells in ruined cities, in houses which no one inhabits, which are ready to become heaps. [29] “He is not rich, nor does his power stand, nor does his possession overspread the earth. [30] “He does not turn away from darkness; the flame dries up his branches, and by the breath of <dn>His</dn> mouth he turns aside. [31] “Let him not trust in futile things, deceiving himself, for futility is his reward. [32] “It is accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green. [33] “He shakes off his unripe grape like a vine, and casts off his blossom like an olive tree. [34] “For the company of the profane is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery. [35] “They conceive trouble and bring forth wickedness, and their belly prepares deceit.”

readings.title: Job Reproves His Friends
readings.subtitle: Miserable Comforters Are You All
readings.text: [Job 16:1] Then Iyyoḇ answered and said, [2] “I have heard many such things; miserable comforters are you all! [3] “Is there an end to windy words? Or what distresses you that you answer? [4] “I could also speak like you, if your soul were in my soul’s place. I could heap up words against you, and shake my head at you; [5] “I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the comfort of my lips would uphold! [6] “If I speak, my pain is not upheld; and if I cease, what goes from me? [7] “But now <dn>He</dn> has wearied me; <dn>You</dn> have stunned all my company. [8] “And <dn>You</dn> have shrivelled me up – it has become a witness; and my leanness rises up against me and bears witness to my face. [9] “<dn>His</dn> wrath has torn, and <dn>He</dn> hates me; <dn>He</dn> has gnashed at me with <dn>His</dn> teeth; my adversary sharpens His eyes against me. [10] “They have gaped at me with their mouth, they have struck me on the cheek reproachfully, they gather themselves together against me. [11] “<dn>El</dn> delivers me to the perverse, and hands me over to the hands of the wrong. [12] “I was at ease, but <dn>He</dn> broke me apart; and <dn>He</dn> took me by my neck and shook me to pieces, and set me up for <dn>His</dn> target, [13] “<dn>His</dn> archers surround me. <dn>He</dn> splits my kidneys and does not spare; <dn>He</dn> pours out my gall on the ground. [14] “<dn>He</dn> breaks me with breach upon breach; <dn>He</dn> runs upon me like a mighty man. [15] “I have sewn sackcloth over my skin, and I have thrust my horn in the dust. [16] “My face is reddened with weeping, and on my eyelids is the shadow of death; [17] “Although no violence is in my hands, and my prayer is pure. [18] “O earth, do not cover my blood, and let my cry have no place! [19] “Even now, see, my witness is in the heavens, and my voucher is on high. [20] “My friends are my mockers; my eye pours out tears to <dn>Eloah</dn>. [21] “And <dn>He</dn> pleads for a man with <dn>Eloah</dn>, as a son of man for his friend. [22] “For years of number come, and I go the way I do not return.
